--- a/tests/test_merge_config_regression.py
+++ b/tests/test_merge_config_regression.py
@@ -0,0 +1,122 @@
+import copy
+
+from config import merge_config
+
+
+def test_simple_override_preserved():
+    assert merge_config({"a": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": 3}) == {"a": 2, "b": 3}
+    assert merge_config({}, {}) == {}
+
+
+def test_returns_mapping_type():
+    result = merge_config({"a": 1}, {"b": 2})
+    assert isinstance(result, dict)
+
+
+def test_all_keys_from_base_and_overrides():
+    result = merge_config({"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"b": 20, "c": 30})
+    assert result == {"a": 1, "b": 20, "c": 30}
+
+
+def test_keys_only_in_base_preserved():
+    result = merge_config({"only_base": 1}, {"other": 2})
+    assert result["only_base"] == 1
+
+
+def test_keys_only_in_overrides_included():
+    result = merge_config({"a": 1}, {"only_override": 2})
+    assert result["only_override"] == 2
+
+
+def test_nested_mappings_merged_recursively():
+    base = {"db": {"host": "localhost", "port": 5432}}
+    overrides = {"db": {"port": 6543, "user": "admin"}}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    assert result == {"db": {"host": "localhost", "port": 6543, "user": "admin"}}
+
+
+def test_override_wins_at_leaf():
+    base = {"a": {"b": {"c": 1}}}
+    overrides = {"a": {"b": {"c": 2}}}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    assert result["a"]["b"]["c"] == 2
+
+
+def test_deeply_nested_merge():
+    base = {"a": {"b": {"c": 1, "d": 2}}}
+    overrides = {"a": {"b": {"c": 9}}}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    assert result == {"a": {"b": {"c": 9, "d": 2}}}
+
+
+def test_lists_are_replaced_not_concatenated():
+    base = {"items": [1, 2, 3]}
+    overrides = {"items": [4, 5]}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    assert result["items"] == [4, 5]
+
+
+def test_list_replacement_does_not_concatenate():
+    base = {"items": [1, 2]}
+    overrides = {"items": [3]}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    assert len(result["items"]) == 1
+    assert result["items"] == [3]
+
+
+def test_does_not_mutate_base():
+    base = {"a": 1, "nested": {"x": 1}, "items": [1, 2]}
+    snapshot = copy.deepcopy(base)
+    merge_config(base, {"a": 2, "nested": {"y": 2}, "items": [9]})
+    assert base == snapshot
+
+
+def test_does_not_mutate_overrides():
+    overrides = {"a": 2, "nested": {"y": 2}, "items": [9]}
+    snapshot = copy.deepcopy(overrides)
+    merge_config({"a": 1, "nested": {"x": 1}, "items": [1, 2]}, overrides)
+    assert overrides == snapshot
+
+
+def test_result_shares_no_nested_objects_with_base():
+    base = {"nested": {"x": 1}, "items": [1, 2]}
+    result = merge_config(base, {})
+    assert result["nested"] is not base["nested"]
+    assert result["items"] is not base["items"]
+
+
+def test_result_shares_no_nested_objects_with_overrides():
+    overrides = {"nested": {"y": 2}, "items": [9]}
+    result = merge_config({}, overrides)
+    assert result["nested"] is not overrides["nested"]
+    assert result["items"] is not overrides["items"]
+
+
+def test_mutating_result_does_not_affect_inputs():
+    base = {"nested": {"x": 1}, "items": [1, 2]}
+    overrides = {"nested": {"y": 2}, "items": [9]}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    result["nested"]["z"] = 3
+    result["items"].append(99)
+    assert base == {"nested": {"x": 1}, "items": [1, 2]}
+    assert overrides == {"nested": {"y": 2}, "items": [9]}
+
+
+def test_mutating_inputs_does_not_affect_result():
+    base = {"nested": {"x": 1}, "items": [1, 2]}
+    overrides = {"nested": {"y": 2}, "items": [9]}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    base["nested"]["x"] = 100
+    base["items"].append(100)
+    overrides["nested"]["y"] = 200
+    overrides["items"].append(200)
+    assert result == {"nested": {"x": 1, "y": 2}, "items": [9]}
+
+
+def test_nested_result_is_independent_mapping():
+    base = {"a": {"b": 1}}
+    overrides = {"a": {"c": 2}}
+    result = merge_config(base, overrides)
+    assert isinstance(result["a"], dict)
+    assert result["a"] is not base["a"]
+    assert result["a"] is not overrides["a"]

contract_tests: merge_config(base, overrides) returns a mapping containing all keys from base and overrides: test_all_keys_from_base_and_overrides asserts merge_config({"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"b": 20, "c": 30}) == {"a": 1, "b": 20, "c": 30}.

When a key exists in both and both values are mappings, the result is a recursive merge: test_nested_mappings_merged_recursively asserts merge_config({"db": {"host": "localhost", "port": 5432}}, {"db": {"port": 6543, "user": "admin"}}) == {"db": {"host": "localhost", "port": 6543, "user": "admin"}}.

At leaf keys, the override value wins over the base value: test_override_wins_at_leaf asserts merge_config({"a": {"b": {"c": 1}}}, {"a": {"b": {"c": 2}}})["a"]["b"]["c"] == 2; test_deeply_nested_merge asserts merge_config({"a": {"b": {"c": 1, "d": 2}}}, {"a": {"b": {"c": 9}}}) == {"a": {"b": {"c": 9, "d": 2}}}.
Keys present only in overrides are included in the result: test_keys_only_in_overrides_included asserts merge_config({"a": 1}, {"only_override": 2})["only_override"] == 2.
Keys present only in base are preserved in the result: test_keys_only_in_base_preserved asserts merge_config({"only_base": 1}, {"other": 2})["only_base"] == 1.

Lists are replaced by the override list, not concatenated: test_lists_are_replaced_not_concatenated asserts merge_config({"items": [1, 2, 3]}, {"items": [4, 5]})["items"] == [4, 5]; test_list_replacement_does_not_concatenate asserts len(merge_config({"items": [1, 2]}, {"items": [3]})["items"]) == 1 and == [3].
The result does not mutate the base input mapping: test_does_not_mutate_base deep-copies base, calls merge_config, and asserts base == snapshot.
The result does not mutate the overrides input mapping: test_does_not_mutate_overrides deep-copies overrides, calls merge_config, and asserts overrides == snapshot.

The result shares no nested mutable objects with base or overrides; mutating the result does not affect either input: test_result_shares_no_nested_objects_with_base asserts result["nested"] is not base["nested"] and result["items"] is not base["items"]; test_result_shares_no_nested_objects_with_overrides asserts the same against overrides; test_mutating_result_does_not_affect_inputs mutates result["nested"] and result["items"] and asserts both inputs unchanged.

Mutating base or overrides after the call does not affect the previously returned result: test_mutating_inputs_does_not_affect_result mutates base and overrides after the call and asserts result == {"nested": {"x": 1, "y": 2}, "items": [9]}.

Simple (non-nested) overrides continue to work as before: test_simple_override_preserved asserts merge_config({"a": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": 3}) == {"a": 2, "b": 3} and merge_config({}, {}) == {}; test_returns_mapping_type asserts isinstance(merge_config({"a": 1}, {"b": 2}), dict); test_nested_result_is_independent_mapping asserts isinstance(result["a"], dict).

edits.old:
def merge_config(defaults, overrides):
    result = dict(defaults)
    result.update(overrides)
    return result

patches.rationale: The original merge_config does a shallow dict update, so overrides never win at nested leaves, lists are not replaced correctly when base has the key, and nested objects are shared. Rewrite it to recursively merge mappings, deep-copy leaves, and build a fresh result. Add a new regression test file (tests/test_merge_config_regression.py is not in existing_test_paths, so it is allowed) covering every acceptance contract with exact inputs and result types.
